extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs) assigned to incidents as members or assistant PIOs on All-Hazards Incident Management Teams (AHIMTs) and local IMTs; personnel regularly assigned to Functional, Support, or Unit Leader positions on Type 3 or 4 AHIMTs or those seeking credentials/certification
extracted.subtask_description: Instructor-led five-day course to develop core Public Information Officer (PIO) skills and the ability to apply them in an All-Hazards Incident Management Team (AHIMT) context, combining basic and advanced PIO functions with scenario-driven exercises and a final exam. Intended for PIOs and assistant PIOs operating on AHIMTs or local IMTs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended roles / course audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed for a Public Information Officer (PIO) assigned to an incident as a member of an All-Hazards Incident Management Team (AHIMT) and local IMTs, as well as for the PIO assigned to an incident as an Assistant PIO in a variety of capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this course when preparing personnel who will serve as PIOs or assistant PIOs on AHIMTs/local IMTs; course scope assumes operational PIO roles within incident management teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core PIO skills development
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will help participants develop a strong set of core PIO skills and the ability to apply them within the context of an AHIMT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on both practical skill acquisition and application within team-based incident management; training outcomes are skills-focused rather than purely theoretical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined basic and advanced functions focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The course is distinct from other information function courses in that it combines elements from both the basic and advanced functions to concentrate training on the fundamental duties and responsibilities of the PIO in an all-hazards environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum intentionally integrates foundational and advanced topics to address the full range of PIO duties in all-hazards settings rather than only entry-level or only advanced topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed participant experience level
rubrics_metrics.description: The course material does not assume or require experience as a PIO, but also is not a basic PIO course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable for learners without prior PIO experience who can handle an accelerated, mixed-level curriculum; not targeted at absolute beginners expecting an introductory-only curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional format and pedagogical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: This course is an instructor-led training that supports learning through discussion, lecture, and active participation in multiple exercises that provides a realistic, scenario-driven approach to mastering the skills required of a PIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect interactive, scenario-based instruction: discussions, lectures, active exercises and simulations are core delivery methods to build practical competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises, simulations, and practice-based assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises, simulations, discussions, and a final exam enable participants to process and apply their new knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment is both formative (exercises, simulations, discussions) and summative (final exam); practical performance in scenario-driven activities is a key measure of competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program area alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Area(s): Citizen Preparedness; Incident Command System; Universal Emergency Preparedness; FEMA Employee Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course content aligns with FEMA/NIMS program areas and is appropriate for use in broader emergency preparedness and ICS professional development tracks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience recommendation / position suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS ICS All-Hazards training should be completed by personnel who are regularly assigned to Functional, Support, or Unit Leader positions on Type 3 or 4 AHIMTs, or by those persons who desire to seek credentials/certification in those positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend enrollment for staff in these specific roles or those pursuing formal credentials; indicates expected organizational roles that will benefit most from the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and workload
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for a full five-day commitment totaling approximately 31 contact hours when scheduling staff; use duration to estimate training resource needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing education and college credit
rubrics_metrics.description: CEUs: 3.5; ACE: Level: Lower Division/Associate; ACE: Credit Hours: 2; ACE: Curriculum: Emergency Management or Public Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course carries continuing education units and lower-division college credit recognition useful for professional development and transcript/credit reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Pre-requisites: E/G0300, ICS-300: Intermediate Incident Command System for Expanding Incidents; E/G0400, ICS-400: Advanced Incident Command System for Command and General Staff—Complex Incidents; IS-0100.b, Introduction to the Incident Command System, ICS-100; IS-0200.b, Incident Command System for Single Resources and Initial Action Incidents; IS-0700.a, National Incident Management System, An Introduction; and IS-0800.b, National Response Framework, An Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are expected to have completed these foundational ICS/NIMS courses prior to enrollment; verify prerequisite completion during registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course materials and job aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials: NIMS ICS All-Hazards Public Information Officer Training Manual; Scenario handouts; EMSI All Hazards Public Information Officer (PIO) Job Aid (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these materials to learners; optional job aids can supplement instruction and on-the-job reference after training.
